baseline_plan.title: Weight blanket edge with books
baseline_plan.summary: Place a stack of books on the overhanging edge of the blanket on the office chair to prevent it from shifting.

steps.action: Drape blanket over office chair seat so that one edge extends beyond the seat.
steps.why_it_helps: Positions the blanket ready for weighting.

steps.action: Place the stack of books on the overhanging blanket edge to weigh it down.
steps.why_it_helps: The weight of the books holds the blanket edge in place, preventing shift.

assumptions: Blanket is large enough to overhang the chair seat.
Books have sufficient mass to act as a weight.
Chair seat surface is flat and stable enough to support books without sliding.
unresolved_risks: Books may slide off if not balanced.
Chair may roll if not locked, causing blanket to shift.
Blanket may still shift if weight insufficient.
constraint_check: Used only inventory objects: office_chair_01, blanket_01, books_01.
No tape, adhesives, fasteners, clamps, or unlisted objects used.
No permanent modifications made to any object.
No damage to any listed object.
Did not rely on unknown liquid contents (spray bottles not used).
Did not rely on electrical properties (power strip not used).
Books used as weight have physical evidence (known mass).

zero_initial_plan.title: Blanket edge stabilizer
zero_initial_plan.summary: Use a stack of books as a weight to hold one edge of the blanket in place on the office chair seat.

steps.action: Place the stack of books on the blanket edge resting on the office chair seat to weigh it down.

capability_uses.purpose: Hold blanket edge down to prevent shifting

steps.why_it_helps: Weighted books create downward force that stops the blanket edge from sliding on the chair seat.

constraint_check: No tape, adhesives, fasteners, clamps used
No damage to any listed object
No reliance on unknown liquid contents
Weight use supported by books' provide_weight capability

findings.claim: Weighted books create downward force that stops blanket edge sliding on chair seat.
findings.explanation: The plan asserts weight prevents sliding, but no trait or capability establishes friction or slip resistance; weight alone does not guarantee edge stability.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a known friction-enhancing method (e.g., fold blanket edge under chair leg) or verify that existing friction suffices before relying on weight alone.

zero_final_plan.title: Blanket edge stabilizer with weight and tuck
zero_final_plan.summary: Use books as weight and tuck the blanket edge under the chair leg to secure it via mechanical interlock.

steps.action: Place the stack of books on the blanket edge resting on the office chair seat to weigh it down.

capability_uses.purpose: Hold blanket edge down to increase normal force

steps.why_it_helps: Added weight raises normal force, which may increase friction if the blanket and seat surfaces are not slippery.

steps.action: Tuck the folded blanket edge under the front leg of the office chair to secure it.

capability_uses.purpose: Create a folded edge to tuck under chair leg
Provide a surface to hold the folded edge

steps.why_it_helps: Tucking the folded edge under the chair leg creates a mechanical interlock that holds the edge.

findings.claim: Tucking creates a mechanical interlock that holds the blanket edge.
findings.explanation: The plan asserts a hold from tucking, but only fold and support capabilities are verified; no evidence shows the interlock prevents slipping.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace claim with that tucking secures edge via friction or geometry, or add a capability like 'hold' if justified.

findings.claim: Blanket is large enough to overhang the chair seat.
findings.explanation: The plan assumes the blanket is large enough to overhang the chair seat, but size is not established in inventory.
